why: Quote is VERBATIM (admin-setup.md:95, a three-column table row whose key column is `processWrapper`; I read the whole line and the surrounding table - no second-sentence reversal, and the adjacent row 'Disable agent view' confirms the launcher is offered as the alternative to disabling background agents). The identifier half of the finding is also correct: MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534 is exactly the cited range, holds 32 keys, and none is `processWrapper` or any launcher key. But the finding is refuted on its CONSEQUENCE, which is the part this repo's audit history says keeps being wrong, and on two of the three process classes it names. (1) 'no launcher-prefix path anywhere in source' is FALSE. packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23 resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher resolves absolute paths for sandbox-exec/bwrap/firejail/unshare, and filesystem-isolation.ts:113/263/313 plus network-isolation.ts:15/27/65 build exactly a launcher-prefixed argv. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts then spawns `plan?.command ?? request.command` (:245) - the ISOLATION-REWRITTEN command - and its own comment at :232-234 says the recorded string is 'The REQUESTED command line, before isolation rewrote it into a sandbox invocation'. A host-owned path that prefixes a child process with a launcher exists and is live. (2) 'the session MCP server ... spawned directly' is FALSE. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:724 starts stdio MCP servers through `this.authority.processSupervisor.start({...})` (port typed at :108), i.e. through the same supervisor chokepoint, with a host-only pre-spawn gate documented at process-supervisor-port.ts:63 as running 'after isolation resolution and immediately before spawn'. (3) The doc row's own scope is 'the background-agent supervisor, ITS WORKERS, and the other covered background processes' - our workers are not OS processes at all: subagents and workflows are in-process child sessions (orchestrator/subtask.ts:95, workflow-tool.ts:358 and :390, review-tool.ts:309, guardian-runner.ts:71), so for that half there is no process to prefix. Only 'the headless server' survives as spawned directly (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:63, Bun.spawn(['bun','run',serverEntry])). The second evidence anchor is also misdescribed: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236 IS buildClaudeSubprocessEnv, but it returns a NodeJS.ProcessEnv and never spawns anything - it cannot be evidence that something 'spawns unwrapped' - and it sits on the Claude backend, which ships off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE). Also inaccurate: 'one spec mention' in docs - there are two lines in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md (:715 and :725) besides the sweep artifacts, and :715 already scoped this as 'Adjacent and worth a decision, not necessarily a build', with :727 recording the reason - 'The corporate-launcher half is the weakest part for us, since it is written against the CLI's own supervisor architecture, which we do not have.' Checked the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3: this is NOT one of them, and it is not a product-difference artifact of the de-brand either (a launcher is if anything MORE relevant to a bank fork), so the narrow residual gap below is real and stays open - but the finding as written overstates it by asserting an absent mechanism and an unenforceable mandate where a host-owned interposition point already exists and already rewrites argv.
correctedState: No admin-configurable corporate-launcher key exists: MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534, 32 keys) carries no `processWrapper` equivalent, and grep -a across packages+apps finds no CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER, processWrapper, shellPrefix or NESSY_-prefixed analogue in source (the only `execWrapper` hit, claude-bash-rule.ts:227/324/337/381, is an unrelated bash-permission-rule parser flag for xargs/find -exec in a sibling subsystem). What is missing is therefore the ADMIN-FACING CONFIGURATION, not the mechanism: a launcher-prefix path already exists and is live for supervised children - resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher (session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23) plus filesystem-/network-isolation build a launcher-prefixed argv, and ProcessSupervisor spawns the rewritten `plan?.command ?? request.command` (server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:245) behind a host-only beforeStart gate (process-supervisor-port.ts:63). Stdio MCP servers route through that chokepoint (shared/src/mcp/client.ts:724), so they are NOT spawned directly. The doc row's 'workers' have no analogue as OS processes here - subagents and workflows are in-process child sessions (orchestrator/subtask.ts:95, workflow-tool.ts:358/390). The genuinely unwrapped class is the headless server, spawned directly at apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:63. Scope already recorded at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:715 ('worth a decision, not necessarily a build') and :727; the decision is owed, not taken.
